newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tests on Russia's new Su-32 fighter near end -Tass.
newsitem.headline: Tests on Russia's new Su-32 fighter near end -Tass.

text.p: The Russian air force is in the process of completing tests on a new jet fighter, the Sukhoi Su-32, nicknamed the "Weapon of the 21st Century", Itar-Tass news agency said on Sunday, quoting an air force spokesman.
Officials at the air force and the Sukhoi aircraft company were not immediately available to confirm the report.

"Tests are being completed in Russia on the multi-role Su-32 warplane, which in the West is called 'the Weapon of the 21st Century," Tass said. "In terms of fighting characteristics, it significantly outperforms the American F15-E."
Development of the new Sukhoi has been shrouded in secrecy and the Tass report suggested that work on the Su-32 may be more advanced than some Western analysts have assumed.
Last week the respected Jane's Defence Weekly quoted Russian sources as saying only that a prototype of the Su-32, which has distinctive swept-forward wings, would first fly "this year".
Defence analysts speculate it will replace Sukhoi's own Su-27 "Flanker", a mainstay of Russia frontline forces since the early 1980s.
In its brief report, the state-controlled Tass agency noted that the Su-32 might be available for export and noted the success of Sukhoi in selling planes like the Su-24 fighter-bomber abroad.
Moscow is pushing to increase the foreign earnings of its arms industry, which was at the forefront of Soviet technology during the Cold War.

Russian officials have also been keen to remind Western politicians, whose plans to expand the NATO defence alliance into eastern Europe are hotly contested by Moscow, that Russia continues to maintain its own powerful defences.
"Russian flyers are waiting for the new plane, seeing in it a real expansion of the air force's military capabilities in ensuring Russia's national security," Tass said.
NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana arrives in Moscow on Sunday for talks aimed at finding a compromise with Russia over the alliance's expansion project.
